primary_source.paper: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them

trace_source: vendor/BIG-Bench-Hard/cot-prompts/boolean_expressions.txt (commit 9ee07bd481feebf959a6b59d61ea57bdcf30964d), first full few-shot exemplar, saved verbatim to published_trace.txt
format_description: Each step is a sentence naming and reducing one named sub-expression, e.g. "Let's evaluate A: A = not not True = not (not True) = not False = True.", with innermost sub-expressions evaluated first and then substituted back into the parent expression in a final 'Plugging in ...' sentence that states the answer.
theory_citation: Buss, S.R. 1987, 'The Boolean Formula Value Problem Is in ALOGTIME,' STOC 1987 -- established Boolean formula evaluation as the canonical NC1-complete (ALOGTIME-complete) problem.

knob.name: nesting depth / operator count
knob.granularity: integer; canonical BBH examples use roughly 4-8 operators. google/BIG-bench's task.py generator (SOURCING.md candidate) exposes expression_lengths directly, tuple-valued, 1-14 (complexity exponential in length)

published_data.metric: few-shot answer-only (AO) vs few-shot CoT accuracy on the 250 canonical BBH boolean_expressions examples, plus random baseline, prior BIG-Bench SOTA, and human-rater avg/max for this task
published_data.values: random=50.0%, prior_BIG-Bench_SOTA=68.5%, human_avg=79.4%, human_max=100%; InstructGPT AO=90.0%->CoT=87.6%; Codex AO=88.4%->CoT=92.8% (cross-checked exactly against vendored code-davinci-002 eval_metrics.jsonl); PaLM-540B AO=83.2%->CoT=80.0%

published_data.paper: google/BIG-bench boolean_expressions task README (vendor/BIG-bench-google), pre-CoT era
published_data.metric: GPT-2-XL accuracy at two expression_lengths settings of the task's own generator knob, vs a small (n=6) human baseline; no CoT prompting existed at time of this eval

notes: tokens_per_step / tokens_total measured with real tokenizers loaded via huggingface_hub + tokenizers on published_trace.txt's CoT completion (the 'A: ...' portion only; 2 reduction steps in this particular exemplar -- 'Let's evaluate A: ...' and the final 'Plugging in A, we get: ...' sentence -- since this trace's expression only has one named sub-expression to resolve before the top-level combination): gemma2 tokenizer.json from unsloth/gemma-2-2b (ungated mirror of google/gemma-2-2b, 401 gated), llama3 tokenizer.json from NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3-8B (ungated mirror of meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B, also 401 gated), qwen2 tokenizer.json from Qwen/Qwen2-7B directly (ungated). state_atomic_tokens=true verified empirically: 'True', 'False', 'not', 'and', 'or' (space-prefixed, as they appear mid-sentence) each encode as exactly one token across all three tokenizers. tokens_flat_across_knob left null rather than guessed: each reduction sentence's length depends on how much of the parent expression must be re-quoted in the 'Z = ... = ...' framing, which was not measured across a range of depths in this pass (deferred implementation work). Canonical BBH boolean_expressions has a binary True/False answer space -- an expected property of the canonical published task, not a defect (a richer non-binary variant would be a separate slug, out of scope for these desk metrics per AMENDMENT 2's instruction to describe the task AS PUBLISHED). contamination_risk medium: the 250 canonical BBH examples are mirrored across at least 6 HuggingFace dataset repos found during search (lukaemon/bbh, maveriq/bigbenchhard, Joschka/big_bench_hard, SaylorTwift/bbh, RUCAIBox/bbh, GPTTT/bigbenchhard) and are almost certainly in recent pretraining corpora. Calibration point from Table 3: CoT does NOT help (and slightly hurts) 2 of 3 model families on this task (InstructGPT 90.0%->87.6%, PaLM 540B 83.2%->80.0%; only Codex improves), and all three are already above the 79.4% human average with answer-only prompting alone -- the canonical difficulty is near-ceiling, a fact worth carrying into any later generator-design phase.
